answer: Recency-decayed standing resists sybils: an identity's influence decays exponentially with each epoch of inactivity, so weight must be continuously re-earned by fresh work. A farmer can spin up a grove of clones, but keeping their aggregate standing alive means paying the full honest workload for every one each epoch — let any sit idle and its weight erodes like karst under slow water. A one-burst gale of fake activity spikes then bleeds to nothing. Maintaining a thousand warm identities costs a thousand continuous efforts, erasing the free-clone multiplier.
